# grepr_datadog_integration (Resource)

Manages a Datadog integration, used by pipelines to receive Datadog agent data and send data back to Datadog. Secrets are written through dedicated endpoints after the integration is saved. They are sensitive but stored in Terraform state. They are write-only: the API never returns them, so a change made outside Terraform is not detected. Removing a secret from the configuration stops managing it without deleting it remotely. If a secret is rejected while the integration is being created, Terraform marks the integration tainted; run `terraform untaint` and apply again to retry the secret without replacing the integration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "datadog_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "datadog_app_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "grepr_datadog_integration" "main" {
  name    = "production_datadog"
  site    = "datadoghq.com"
  api_key = var.datadog_api_key
  app_key = var.datadog_app_key
}

variable "datadog_legacy_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Several API keys, all accepted for inbound data; one sends data to Datadog.
# After importing an integration, existing keys can be kept by key_id alone.
resource "grepr_datadog_integration" "multi_key" {
  name = "multi_key_datadog"
  site = "datadoghq.com"

  api_keys = {
    primary = { value = var.datadog_api_key, send_key = true }
    legacy  = { value = var.datadog_legacy_api_key, label = "legacy agents" }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Integration name.
- `site` (String) Datadog site, such as `datadoghq.com`. Must be one of the organization's allowed sites.

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) API key used to send data to Datadog, validated with Datadog. Saving it rotates the send key and is refused while a pipeline using the integration is running. Conflicts with `api_keys`.
- `api_keys` (Attributes Map) The integration's entire API key set, keyed by stable labels; reordering does not rotate keys, but renaming a label re-creates that key under a new ID. Keys added outside Terraform are removed the next time Terraform writes the set. Exactly one entry sets `send_key`. Holds 1–64 entries, and the organization's key quota (10 by default) also applies. Removing the attribute stops managing the set without deleting keys. Conflicts with `api_key`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_keys))
- `app_key` (String, Sensitive) Application key. Grepr checks its scopes with Datadog, which needs the API key saved first.
- `dashboard_freshness_window` (String) Import only dashboards viewed within this ISO-8601 duration, written in the server's form such as `PT720H` for 30 days; another spelling shows as a change. Omit to import every dashboard.
- `include_never_viewed_dashboards` (Boolean) Also import dashboards that were never viewed.
- `team_ids` (Set of String) Team IDs with access. Omit to keep the current teams; an empty set clears them.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Integration ID.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization owning the integration.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update timestamp.
- `version` (Number) Integration version used for optimistic locking.

<a id="nestedatt--api_keys"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_keys`

Optional:

- `key_id` (String) Existing key ID, or the ID the server assigns to a new key. Omit it for a new key.
- `label` (String) Display label. Omission clears the remote label.
- `send_key` (Boolean) Use this key to send data to Datadog.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) Plaintext key. Required for a new key; omit to keep an existing key by `key_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import grepr_datadog_integration.main INTEGRATION_ID
```
